solution: The circle \(x^{2} + y^{2} = 4\) has radius \(2\), so in the first quadrant it runs from \(x = 0\) to \(x = 2\); the lines \(x = 0\) and \(x = 2\) are exactly the two bounding ordinates, so the region is the full first-quadrant quarter disc. Area \(= \tfrac{1}{4}\pi r^{2} = \tfrac{1}{4}\pi(4) = \pi\). Equivalently \(\int_{0}^{2}\sqrt{4-x^{2}}\,dx = \left[\tfrac{x\sqrt{4-x^{2}}}{2} + 2\sin^{-1}\tfrac{x}{2}\right]_{0}^{2} = 0 + 2\left(\tfrac{\pi}{2}\right) = \pi\).

The region is bounded by the \(y\)-axis, so integrate with respect to \(y\): \(y^{2} = 4x\) gives \(x = \tfrac{y^{2}}{4}\). Area \(= \int_{0}^{3}\tfrac{y^{2}}{4}\,dy = \left[\tfrac{y^{3}}{12}\right]_{0}^{3} = \tfrac{27}{12} = \tfrac{9}{4} = 2.25\). The value \(\tfrac{9}{3} = 3\) is the trap of dividing by \(3\) instead of \(12\).

\(y = x^{3}\) is negative on \((-2, 0)\) and positive on \((0, 1)\), so AREA requires the absolute value on each side separately, not one signed integral. \(\left|\int_{-2}^{0}x^{3}\,dx\right| = \left|0 - \tfrac{16}{4}\right| = 4\) and \(\int_{0}^{1}x^{3}\,dx = \tfrac{1}{4}\), giving a total of \(4 + \tfrac{1}{4} = \tfrac{17}{4}\). Verified by numeric midpoint integration of \(\left|x^{3}\right|\) over \([-2, 1]\) with 2,000,000 subintervals: \(4.2499999999988\), matching \(\tfrac{17}{4} = 4.25\). The value \(-\tfrac{15}{4}\) is the signed integral \(-4 + \tfrac{1}{4}\) and is the trap; a negative area is impossible, which also rules out \(-9\) and \(-\tfrac{15}{4}\) on sight.

\(y = x|x|\) equals \(x^{2}\) for \(x > 0\) and \(-x^{2}\) for \(x < 0\), so the curve lies below the axis on \((-1, 0)\) and above it on \((0, 1)\). Area \(= \left|\int_{-1}^{0}-x^{2}\,dx\right| + \int_{0}^{1}x^{2}\,dx = \tfrac{1}{3} + \tfrac{1}{3} = \tfrac{2}{3}\). Verified by numeric midpoint integration of \(\left|\,x|x|\,\right|\) over \([-1, 1]\) with 1,000,000 subintervals: \(0.66666666667\), matching \(\tfrac{2}{3}\). The value \(0\) is the signed integral of this odd function, i.e. the trap.
